children.heading: Citrus disease subcommittee
children.text: The term “citrus disease subcommittee” means the subcommittee established under section 3123a(a)(2) of this title.

children.heading: Initiative
children.text: The term “Initiative” means the specialty crop research and extension initiative established by subsection (b).

children.heading: Specialty crop
children.text: The term “specialty crop” has the meaning given that term in section 3 of the Specialty Crops Competitiveness Act of 2004 (7 U.S.C. 1621 note; Public Law 108–465).

children.heading: Specialty crops committee
children.text: The term “specialty crops committee” means the committee established under section 3123a of this title.

tree.heading: Establishment
tree.text: There is established within the Department a specialty crop research and extension initiative to address the critical needs of the specialty crop industry by developing and disseminating science-based tools to address needs of specific crops and their regions, including—

children.text: research in plant breeding, genetics, genomics, and other methods to improve crop characteristics, such as—
product, taste, quality, and appearance;
size-controlling rootstock systems for perennial crops;
environmental responses and tolerances;
nutrient management, including plant nutrient uptake efficiency;
pest and disease management, including resistance to pests and diseases resulting in reduced application management strategies; and
enhanced phytonutrient content;
efforts to identify and address threats from pests and diseases, including—
threats to specialty crop pollinators;
emerging and invasive species; and
a more effective understanding and utilization of existing natural enemy complexes;
efforts—
to improve production efficiency, handling and processing, productivity, and profitability over the long term (including specialty crop policy and marketing); and
to achieve a better understanding of—
the soil rhizosphere microbiome;
pesticide application systems and certified drift-reduction technologies; and
systems to improve and extend the storage life of specialty crops;
new innovations and technology, including—
mechanization and automation of labor-intensive tasks in production and processing;
technologies that delay or inhibit ripening;
decision support systems driven by phenology and environmental factors;
improved monitoring systems for agricultural pests; and
effective systems for preharvest and postharvest management of quarantine pests; and
methods to prevent, detect, monitor, control, and respond to potential food safety hazards in the production and processing of specialty crops, including fresh produce.

tree.heading: Eligible entities
tree.text: The Secretary may carry out this section through—

children.text: Federal agencies;
national laboratories;
colleges and universities;
research institutions and organizations;
private organizations or corporations;
State agricultural experiment stations;
individuals; or
groups consisting of 2 or more entities described in paragraphs (1) through (7).

tree.heading: Review of proposals
tree.text: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall award competitive grants on the basis of—

children.text: a scientific peer review conducted by a panel of subject matter experts from Federal agencies, non-Federal entities, and the specialty crop industry; and
a review and ranking for merit, relevance, and impact conducted by a panel of specialty crop industry representatives for the specific specialty crop.

tree.heading: Consultation
tree.text: Each fiscal year, before conducting the scientific peer review described in paragraph (1) of subsection (d) and the merit and relevancy review described in paragraph (2) of such subsection, the Secretary shall consult with the specialty crops committee regarding such reviews. The committee shall provide the Secretary—

children.text: in the first fiscal year in which that consultation occurs, any recommendations for conducting such reviews in such fiscal year; and
in any subsequent fiscal year in which such consultation occurs—
an assessment of the procedures and objectives used by the Secretary for such reviews in the previous fiscal year;
any recommendations for such reviews for the current fiscal year; and
any comments on grants awarded under subsection (d) during the previous fiscal year.

tree.heading: Report
tree.text: The Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report on—

children.text: the results of the consultations with the specialty crops committee (and subcommittees thereof) conducted under subsection (e) of this section and subsection (g) of section 3123a of this title;
the specialty crops committee’s (and subcommittees thereof) recommendations, if any, provided to the Secretary during such consultations; and
the specialty crops committee’s (and subcommittees thereof) review of the grants awarded under subsection (d) and (j), as applicable, in the previous fiscal year.

children.heading: In general
children.text: With respect to grants awarded under this section, the Secretary shall seek and accept proposals for grants.

children.heading: Term
children.text: The term of a grant under this section may not exceed 10 years.

children.heading: In general
children.text: An entity receiving a grant under this section shall provide non-Federal matching funds (including funds from an agricultural commodity promotion, research, and information program) equal to not less than the amount of the grant.

children.heading: In-kind support
children.text: Non-Federal matching funds described in subparagraph (A) may include in-kind support.

children.heading: Other conditions
children.text: The Secretary may set such other conditions on the award of a grant under the Initiative as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

tree.heading: Priorities
tree.text: In making grants under the Initiative, the Secretary shall provide a higher priority to projects that—

children.text: are multistate, multi-institutional, or multidisciplinary; and
include explicit mechanisms to communicate results to producers and the public.

tree.heading: Buildings and facilities
tree.text: Funds made available under this section shall not be used for the construction of a new building or facility or the acquisition, expansion, remodeling, or alteration of an existing building or facility (including site grading and improvement, and architect fees).

tree.heading: Emergency citrus disease research and extension program

children.heading: Establishment and purpose
children.text: The Secretary shall establish a competitive research and extension grant program to combat diseases of citrus under which the Secretary awards competitive grants to eligible entities—

to conduct scientific research and extension activities, technical assistance, and development activities to combat citrus diseases and pests, both domestic and invasive, which pose imminent harm to the United States citrus production and threaten the future viability of the citrus industry, including huanglongbing and the Asian Citrus Psyllid; and
to provide support for the dissemination and commercialization of relevant information, techniques, and technologies discovered pursuant to research and extension activities funded through—
the emergency citrus disease research and extension program; or
other research and extension projects intended to solve problems caused by citrus production diseases and invasive pests.

children.heading: Priority
children.text: In awarding grants under this subsection, the Secretary shall give priority to grants that address the research and extension priorities established pursuant to subsection (g)(4) of section 3123a of this title.

children.heading: Coordination
children.text: When developing the proposed research and extension agenda and budget under subsection (g)(2) of section 3123a of this title for the funds made available under this subsection for a fiscal year, the citrus disease subcommittee shall—
seek input from Federal and State agencies and other entities involved in citrus disease response; and
take into account other public and private citrus-related research and extension projects and the funding for such projects.

children.heading: Nonduplication
children.text: The Secretary shall ensure that funds made available to carry out the emergency citrus disease research and extension activities under this subsection shall be in addition to and not supplant funds made available to carry out other citrus disease activities carried out by the Department of Agriculture in consultation with State agencies.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations
children.text: In addition to the amounts reserved under subsection (k)(1)(C), there are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this subsection, $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018.

children.heading: Definitions
children.text: In this subsection:

children.heading: Citrus
children.text: The term “citrus” means edible fruit of the family Rutaceae, including any hybrid of such fruits and products of such hybrids that are produced for commercial purposes in the United States.

children.heading: Citrus producer
children.text: The term “citrus producer” means any person that is engaged in the domestic production and commercial sale of citrus in the United States.

children.heading: Emergency citrus disease research and extension program
children.text: The term “emergency citrus disease research and extension program” means the emergency citrus research and extension grant program established under this subsection.

children.heading: Fiscal years 2008 through 2012
children.text: Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall make available to carry out this section $30,000,000 for fiscal year 2008 and $50,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2009 through 2012, from which activities under each of paragraphs (1) through (5) of subsection (b) shall be allocated not less than 10 percent.

children.heading: Subsequent funding
children.text: Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall make available to carry out this section—
$80,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2025; and
$175,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 and each fiscal year thereafter.

children.heading: Reservation
children.text: For each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018, the Secretary shall reserve not less than $25,000,000 of the funds made available under subparagraph (B) to carry out the program established under subsection (j).

children.heading: Availability of funds
children.text: Funds reserved under subparagraph (C) shall remain available and reserved for the purpose described in such subparagraph until expended.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations for fiscal years 2014 through 2023
children.text: In addition to funds made available under paragraph (1), there is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $100,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

children.heading: Fiscal year 2013
children.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $100,000,000 for fiscal year 2013.

children.heading: Transfer
children.text: Of the funds made available to the Secretary under paragraph (1) for fiscal year 2008 and authorized for use for payment of administrative expenses under section 3315(a)(3) of this title, the Secretary shall transfer, upon the date of enactment of this section, $200,000 to the Office of Prevention, Pesticides, and Toxic Substances of the Environmental Protection Agency for use in conducting a meta-analysis relating to methyl bromide.

children.heading: Availability
children.text: Funds made available pursuant to this subsection for a fiscal year shall remain available until expended to pay for obligations incurred in that fiscal year.

notes.text: Pub. L. 115–334, title VII, § 7610, Dec. 20, 2018, 132 Stat. 4830, provided that: “(a) In General.—Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act [Dec. 20, 2018], the Secretary [of Agriculture] shall conduct a review of the programs of the Department of Agriculture that affect the production or processing of specialty crops. “(b) Requirements.—The review under subsection (a) shall identify—“(1) programs that currently are, or previously have been, effectively used to accelerate the development and use of automation or mechanization in the production or processing of specialty crops; and “(2) programs that may be more effectively used to accelerate the development and use of automation or mechanization in the production or processing of specialty crops. “(c) Strategy.—With respect to programs identified under subsection (b), the Secretary shall develop and implement a strategy to accelerate the development and use of automation and mechanization in the production or processing of specialty crops.”
